facts.quote: The Home Depot®, the world's largest home improvement retailer, today reported sales of $47.9 billion for the second quarter of fiscal 2026, an increase of $2.6 billion, or 5.7% from the second quarter of fiscal 2025.

Guidance includes IEEPA tariff refunds, which are expected to partially offset unplanned fuel, energy, and other product input costs throughout the fiscal year. •Total sales growth of approximately 2.5% to 4.5% •Comparable sales growth of approximately flat to 2.0% •Approximately 15 new stores •Gross margin of approximately 33.1% •Operating margin of approximately 12.4% to 12.6% •Adjusted(1) operating margin of approximately 12.8% to 13.0% •Effective tax rate of approximately 24.3% •Net interest expense of approximately $2.3 billion •Diluted earnings-per-share to grow approximately flat to 4.0% from $14.23 in fiscal 2025

traps: GAAP diluted EPS is $4.79; adjusted (non-GAAP) diluted EPS is $4.92 and excludes only acquired intangible asset amortization net of tax. Reporting $4.92 without the adjusted label misstates the release.
Three growth rates sit side by side: total sales up 5.7%, comparable sales up 1.7%, U.S. comparable sales up 1.3%. Swapping them is the easiest error.

Quarter vs six months: the statement of earnings carries six-month columns ($89,626 million sales, $8.09 diluted EPS), the non-GAAP reconciliation table carries the six-month 13.2% operating margin, and the cash flow statement is six months only, so there is no quarterly operating cash flow or dividend figure.
Fiscal calendar: the second quarter of fiscal 2026 ended August 2, 2026, compared with the quarter ended August 3, 2025; fiscal 2025 ended February 1, 2026.
Units: tables are in millions (per share data excepted); the text rounds to $47.9 billion sales and $4.8 billion net earnings.

Guidance was reaffirmed, not raised. GAAP and adjusted EPS guidance are both flat to 4.0% growth, but from different bases ($14.23 GAAP, $14.69 adjusted); operating margin guidance is 12.4% to 12.6% GAAP and 12.8% to 13.0% adjusted.
Operating margin contracted (14.3% vs 14.5% GAAP; 14.7% vs 14.8% adjusted) even though sales grew 5.7%; the release prints no quarterly gross margin percentage, and 33.1% is full-year guidance.
The release reports no business segments, no share repurchases, and no dividend declaration; any segment breakdown or buyback figure is invented.
Transaction and ticket measures exclude HD Supply and SRS; comparable transactions fell 1.0% while comparable ticket rose 2.8%.

The acquisition contribution to the gap between 5.7% total growth and 1.7% comps is not quantified in the release; payments for businesses acquired of $1,333 million are six-month cash flows, not a quarterly revenue contribution.
